newsitem.title: USA: Telecom zero junk deal to hit U.S. corp bond mart.
newsitem.headline: Telecom zero junk deal to hit U.S. corp bond mart.

text.p: Telesystems International Wireless Inc, a telecommunications company, is one of several junk bond issuers expected to price a deal in the U.S. corporate bond market on Tuesday, market sources said.
The Telesystems issue will represent the first time in many months that a startup telecommunications company has successfully issued zero-coupon bonds.
Market players say the deal is yet another indication of the strength of the junk bond market.
Market sources said there are $1 billion in orders for the 144A private placement of $200 million (proceeds) of 10-year senior discount notes.

Huge demand for the deal prompted Telesystems and its underwriters, Goldman Sachs & Co and CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp, to dispense with an equity component included in the orginal junk bond offering.
Price talk on the deal, rated Caa1/B-minus, was changed to 13.25 percent from an original 12.25-12.50 percent and warrants to buy up to one percent of the company.
Market sources said investors are applauding Telesystems's business strategy, which is to invest in diverse wireless operations in emerging-market countries.
"There is a perception that these markets are underserved and that this company is tapping into them in the right way. This could be a grand slam," said one portfolio manager.
Three other junk bond deals were expected to price on Tuesday. They include:
- Talton Holdings Inc $100 million 144A private placement of senior notes via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities. Price talk on the notes, rated B2/B, is in the 10.75 percent area.
The company provides phone services to prison inmates.

- Randall's Food Markets plans a private placement of $150 million in 10-year senior notes via BT Securities Corp. Price talk for the deal, rated B2/B-minus, is 300-325 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
- Sinclair Broadcasting Group is expected to sell at least $200 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Smith Barney Inc.
In the primary market for high-grade corporate bonds, action is expected to pick up after a slow start on Monday, syndicate officials said.
Rumors continue to swirl about a potential offering from RJR Nabisco Holdings Inc of $350 million in seven- and 10-year notes via Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley this week.
A Morgan Stanley syndicate official said no transaction is pending. An RJR spokeswoman said that as a matter of policy, the company does not respond to rumors.
Analysts said it is possible that RJR would price a deal amid the current news frenzy over the proposed settlement between the tobacco industry and the U.S. states.
"If you think about it, the market for (tobacco companies) has been volatile for an extended period of time, and will show no sign of changing soon," said one analyst.
"Given the favorable interest rate environment currently, on a relative and absolute basis, it makes sense for them to tap this market," the analyst added.
For Tuesday, IKON Capital Inc, a subsidiary of IKON Office Solutions Inc, plans to sell $150 million of four-year notes, rated A3/A-minus, via Lehman Brothers.
Colorado Interstate Gas, a unit of Coastal Corp, plans to sell $100 million of 40-year notes, puttable in 10 years, via Chase Securities. The notes are rated Baa2/BBB.
